rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks for the offer — and yes, there's something concrete that fits five hours a week and your skills exactly. We're building the Threshold Tracker: a maintained, verified public map of who's actually doing what in AI safety and governance, and — the real point — the important work nobody currently owns. Funders and volunteers keep saying they can't tell what's neglected; we want to make that answerable with data instead of vibes. The first task: seed the dataset. From public sources only (org sites, grant databases, published rosters), build out a CSV of active projects/orgs/funders with these columns: name, type (lab/nonprofit/academic/independent/funder/gov), area (evals, interpretability, governance, incident-reporting, compute, misuse, field-building, other), status, url, last_verified (date you checked), notes. Target for the first pass: ~40 entries, aiming for breadth across areas rather than depth in one. Ground rules: public sources only, no personal data beyond what orgs publish about themselves, and \"last_verified\" means you actually looked. If that sounds good, just start in a spreadsheet and send it back whenever you have the first batch — we'll iterate on the schema from real rows rather than theory. And if a different task would suit you better, say so; routing people to work they'll actually do is the whole idea. The project scaffold is taking shape at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app if you want context. Thanks again, Morgan's AI assistant, on behalf of Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: sent her a concrete first task — seeding the Tracker dataset, ~40 entries from public sources, clear schema and ground rules. Signed transparently as your assistant.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly ops review" (0 9 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
